I haven't read the statement in detail or done any play-testing yet. My feedback below is focused primarily on the high-level presentation and structure of the statement.

* Here's a link to a statement for your reference: https://www.codingame.com/contribute/view/1516179aa763a6302dbdfa2c8676688ed085c3 (click "Test in ide").

* Use <const> instead of <var> to format constants. Use <action> instead of <var> to format action verbs (e.g. PLACE, WAIT).

* Please add separate sections for "League introduction" (at the beginning of the statement) and "League preview" (at the end of the statement). Refer to the linked statement (the green boxes) for the required HTML code.

* Please add separate sections for "Victory Conditions" and "Defeat Conditions" (the teal box and the red box). Refer to the linked statement for the required HTML code.

* If appropriate, consider adding diagrams or images to illustrate the concepts.

* Please apply the appropriate background colour, and the line number text colour for the game input/output section. Refer to… you know :)

* Please specify variable type (e.g. "two space-separated integers", "an integer") and description for all variables in the game input/output section.

* Please change these headings:
  • Initialization => Initialization input
  • Each turn => Input for one game turn
  • Output => Output for one game turn

* Please format the above three and "Constraints" headings properly.

* Constraints: Please split the constraints into individual points, with one constraint per line.

* Consider adding a link to the referee code.

* If the game concept is based on an existing game or another source, please acknowledge and credit the original creator or source.

* Please upload a cover picture for the puzzle.

Thanks.

Hello! **Glintwatch** is a 2-4 player simultaneous bot game. Each player owns a lamp on one edge of a square reef. You place and turn neutral mirrors to bend your beam onto crystals. A crystal pays only the player who lights it alone, and it pays more each turn that player keeps it (x1 up to x4).

**What is new on CodinGame:** we checked the existing bot games and found none built on light beams and mirrors. Every mirror bends every beam, so each move helps or hurts all players at once. The four seats are identical under 90-degree rotation.

**Leagues:** first (place mirrors, every lit crystal pays 1), second (rocks, turning mirrors, solo-lit scoring with streaks, 5-turn locks), third (mirror supply, 2-turn build time with a hidden type, wear after 20 turns), fourth (crystal tides, values 1-3, a +2 strike for a beam ending on a rival lamp). Boss ladder (final boss files, each on its own league's rules, 1v1, 200 seeds, seats rotated, ties count half): each boss beats the boss before it in 100 %, 84.3 % and 100 % of games.

**How it was tested** (4-player tables of 400 games and 1v1 matches of 200 games, fixed seeds, seats rotated; the 3-player mode was not part of these runs):
- our strongest test bot finishes first against three of the third-league boss in 99.5 % of 400 4-player games; with four copies of it, first place by seat is 22.7 / 26.1 / 24.6 / 26.6 % (target 25 +/- 5);
- simple scripted strategies (blocking, spoiling) win at most 3.9 % of games when that bot is at the table;
- a coding agent that saw only the statement wrote a bot in about 30 minutes: it wins 46.3 % of 400 1v1 games against our strongest test bot (chance is 50 %) and 23.5 % first place (ours 26.5 %) in 800 seats of 4-player tables with 2 copies of each;
- time per turn of the top boss (CPU time, 100 games, 19x19): p99 6.8 ms, max 11.3 ms (limit 50 ms). Win rates were measured while the machine ran other jobs (load 6-39); CPU times do not depend on load.

**Known limits:**
- A bot written by a coding agent from the statement in about 30 minutes nearly matches our best bot: the game rewards a good simulation and evaluation more than deep search.
- Extra compute does not help our bots: 3.5x to 10x more search per turn gave 17-28 % first place in 4-player tables (25 % is chance, +/- 2.2 points). A different search may still do better.
- Timings were not yet measured on a quiet machine, and real time (not CPU time) was not measured. The referee's own time per turn was not measured.
- No French statement yet.

**Feedback wanted:** is the statement clear enough to write a first bot? Are the league steps the right size? Is the viewer readable with 4 overlapping beams (colour-blind cues: shapes and beam patterns)?

**How it was made:** I designed and directed this game. The rules, code, art and texts were produced with AI agents working for me under my review. The game, its rules and its assets are original: no other game's code, names or art were used.
